# Tailwind output

`tailwind.css` is for Tailwind CSS v4 (tested against 4.3.3). Turn it off with `tailwind: false` and use `tokens.css` alone.

It is built from the same tokens as `tokens.css` and has up to three sections. This is the complete file the example writes:

<!-- verbatim: examples/basic/generated/tailwind.css -->
```css
/** AUTO-GENERATED by figma-tokens — do not edit. */

/* 1 ─ raw tokens → utilities (primitives: white/black) */
@theme inline {
  --color-primitive-white: var(--color-primitive-white);
  --color-primitive-black: var(--color-primitive-black);
  --color-semantic-light-brand-primary-10: var(--color-semantic-light-brand-primary-10);
  --color-semantic-light-brand-primary: var(--color-semantic-light-brand-primary);
  --color-semantic-light-brand-on-primary: var(--color-semantic-light-brand-on-primary);
  --color-semantic-light-neutral-background: var(--color-semantic-light-neutral-background);
  --color-semantic-light-neutral-on-background: var(--color-semantic-light-neutral-on-background);
  --color-semantic-light-status-error: var(--color-semantic-light-status-error);
  --color-semantic-dark-brand-primary: var(--color-semantic-dark-brand-primary);
  --color-semantic-dark-brand-on-primary: var(--color-semantic-dark-brand-on-primary);
  --color-semantic-dark-neutral-background: var(--color-semantic-dark-neutral-background);
  --color-semantic-dark-neutral-on-background: var(--color-semantic-dark-neutral-on-background);
  --radius-sm: var(--radius-sm);
  --radius-md: var(--radius-md);
  --duration-primary: var(--duration-primary);
  --font-fa-primary: var(--font-fa-primary);
  --size-body: var(--size-body);
  --size-heading-lg: var(--size-heading-lg);
  --font-weight-regular: var(--font-weight-regular);
  --font-weight-bold: var(--font-weight-bold);
}

/* 2 ─ semantic layer: light by default, flips under .dark */
:root {
  --color-brand-primary-10: var(--color-semantic-light-brand-primary-10);
  --color-brand-primary: var(--color-semantic-light-brand-primary);
  --color-brand-on-primary: var(--color-semantic-light-brand-on-primary);
  --color-neutral-background: var(--color-semantic-light-neutral-background);
  --color-neutral-on-background: var(--color-semantic-light-neutral-on-background);
  --color-status-error: var(--color-semantic-light-status-error);
  --font-sans: var(--font-fa-primary);
}

.dark {
  /* --color-brand-primary-10: no dark token in Figma — keeps light value */
  --color-brand-primary: var(--color-semantic-dark-brand-primary);
  --color-brand-on-primary: var(--color-semantic-dark-brand-on-primary);
  --color-neutral-background: var(--color-semantic-dark-neutral-background);
  --color-neutral-on-background: var(--color-semantic-dark-neutral-on-background);
  /* --color-status-error: no dark token in Figma — keeps light value */
}

/* 3 ─ semantic names → utilities */
@theme inline {
  --color-brand-primary-10: var(--color-brand-primary-10);
  --color-brand-primary: var(--color-brand-primary);
  --color-brand-on-primary: var(--color-brand-on-primary);
  --color-neutral-background: var(--color-neutral-background);
  --color-neutral-on-background: var(--color-neutral-on-background);
  --color-status-error: var(--color-status-error);
  --color-primary: var(--color-brand-primary);
  --color-primary-foreground: var(--color-brand-on-primary);
  --color-background: var(--color-neutral-background);
  --color-foreground: var(--color-neutral-on-background);
  --color-destructive: var(--color-status-error);
  --text-body: var(--size-body);
  --text-heading-lg: var(--size-heading-lg);
  --transition-duration-primary: var(--duration-primary);
  --radius: var(--radius-md);
  --font-sans: var(--font-sans);
}
```

---

## Section 1: tokens as theme variables

Each line registers a token with Tailwind: `--radius-md: var(--radius-md);` inside `@theme inline`. The `inline` keyword makes the utility use `var(--radius-md)` itself instead of a copy.

Everything is registered **except the primitive colours** you did not keep (option `primitives.keep`). That is why the example has `--color-primitive-white` and `--color-primitive-black` but not the blue and red. The primitives still exist in `tokens.css`; they only get no utility, so `bg-primitive-blue-500` does not exist and `bg-primitive-white` does.

From this section you get, among others:

| Utility | From | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `rounded-md` | `--radius-md` | `border-radius: var(--radius-md)` |
| `font-regular`, `font-bold` | `--font-weight-*` | `font-weight: var(--font-weight-bold)` |
| `font-fa-primary` | `--font-fa-primary` | `font-family: var(--font-fa-primary)` |
| `bg-primitive-white` | `--color-primitive-white` | `background-color: var(--color-primitive-white)` |
| `bg-semantic-light-brand-primary` | the light variable | the light colour, in both themes |

## Section 2: the semantic layer

`:root` points each semantic name at its **light** variable, and `.dark` points it at the **dark** one:

```css
:root { --color-brand-primary: var(--color-semantic-light-brand-primary); }
.dark { --color-brand-primary: var(--color-semantic-dark-brand-primary); }
```

The rules:

- **The names come from the light group.** One line per light colour, named with the rules in [[Conversion-Rules]].
- **The dark colour is found by name.** `Light → Brand → Primary → $root` and `Dark → Brand → Primary` are both `brand-primary`, whatever the capitals.
- **No dark colour means no override.** The `.dark` block then holds a comment, and the colour stays as in light:

  `/* --color-status-error: no dark token in Figma — keeps light value */`
- **A dark colour with no light one is ignored.**
- If there are no semantic colours and no `fontSans`, section 2 is left out. The selectors are the options `selector` and `darkSelector`.

If `fontSans` is set, `:root` also gets `--font-sans: var(--font-fa-primary);` (with your variable name).

## Section 3: names you use in class names

An `@theme inline` block with, in this order:

1. one line per semantic colour: `--color-brand-primary: var(--color-brand-primary);` → `bg-brand-primary`, `text-brand-primary`, …
2. your `aliases`: `--color-primary: var(--color-brand-primary);` → `bg-primary`
3. one `--text-*` line per size token, so `Size.Body` gives `text-body` and `Size.Heading.Lg` gives `text-heading-lg`
4. one `--transition-duration-*` line per duration token, so `Duration.Primary` gives `duration-primary`
5. your `extra` CSS
6. `--font-sans: var(--font-sans);` when `fontSans` is set, so `font-sans` uses your font

Point 4 matters: in Tailwind 4.3.3 a `--duration-*` variable alone does not create a `duration-*` class, because Tailwind reads `--transition-duration-*`. Without that line, `duration-primary` would not exist.

---

## Dark mode

Putting the class `dark` on an element (normally `<html>`) switches every semantic colour inside it. The utilities read the variables, so no `dark:` prefix is needed:

```html
<html class="dark">
  <body class="bg-background text-foreground">…</body>
</html>
```

The `dark:` **variant** is a different thing. In Tailwind v4 it follows `prefers-color-scheme` unless you redefine it. If you want `dark:bg-card` to follow the class as well, add:

```css
@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));
```

That compiles `dark:bg-background` to `.dark\:bg-background:where(.dark, .dark *)`; the test suite checks it. If you changed `darkSelector`, change the variant to match.

---

## Using the files

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "./generated/tokens.css";
@import "./generated/tailwind.css";
```

`tailwind.css` needs the variables from `tokens.css`, so import both.

The utilities the test suite compiles with Tailwind 4.3.3 and checks are `bg-primary`, `text-primary-foreground`, `bg-background`, `bg-brand-primary-10`, `bg-primitive-white`, `rounded-md`, `duration-primary`, `text-body`, `text-heading-lg`, `font-bold`, `font-regular`, `font-sans`, `font-fa-primary`, and that `bg-primitive-blue-500` does not exist.
